subtitle.zh: 一次关于标签、身体与观看的交互体验
subtitle.en: An interactive exploration of labels, bodies, and the gaze

description.zh: 将疾病污名的研究转译为一条跨越身份生成、求职与直播表演的交互路径。
description.en: Translating research on illness stigma into an interactive journey through identity, recruitment, and livestream performance.

kind.zh: XR／交互体验 · 协作项目

coverAlt.zh: 紫粉色虚拟表演空间，中央人物被舞台与观众视线包围。
coverAlt.en: A pink and purple virtual performance space with a figure at its centre.

role.zh: 交互体验与视觉设计（协作项目）
role.en: Interaction and visual design within a collaborative project

stage.zh: 研究、XR 体验设计与装置原型
stage.en: Research, XR experience design, and installation prototypes

deliverables.zh: 体验路径、交互机制、虚拟场景与直播视觉
deliverables.en: Experience journey, interaction mechanisms, virtual environments, and livestream visuals

overview.zh: 疾病如何从一个人的处境，变成社会评价中的标签？项目围绕污名化、娱乐化与浪漫化三个层面，用连续的交互情境呈现标签如何形成，并影响个体的机会与自我表达。
overview.en: How does an illness become a social label? This project explores stigmatisation, entertainment, and romanticisation through connected scenarios that reveal how labels shape opportunity and self-expression.

paragraphs.zh: 研究材料关注疾病在就业、社交媒体与流行文化中的呈现。同一个标签可能在求职时成为障碍，在直播中被当作表演素材，也可能被包装成一种审美符号。
paragraphs.en: The research examines representations of illness in employment, social media, and popular culture. A label may become a barrier in recruitment, material for a performance, or an aesthetic symbol.

paragraphs.zh: 设计目标是让参与者体验这些评价机制之间的联系，而不只是观看一组关于污名的说明。项目中的身份与评分属于叙事情境，不承担医学诊断功能。
paragraphs.en: The aim is to let participants experience connections between these judgements. Identities and scores are elements of the narrative, rather than medical assessments.

text.zh: 把个体简化为疾病标签，观察标签如何影响招聘判断。
text.en: Reduce an individual to a label and explore how that label influences recruitment decisions.

text.zh: 把身体与行为变成观看、指令与评分的对象。
text.en: Turn bodies and behaviour into objects of viewing, instruction, and rating.

text.zh: 将过程数据转化为审美化的身份肖像，反观这种包装。
text.en: Turn accumulated data into an aesthetic portrait and question the packaging of identity.

paragraphs.zh: 用一条连续路径连接不同媒介。前一环节生成的身份与行为信息，成为下一环节的输入，让标签的影响累积，而不是每个场景重新开始。
paragraphs.en: A continuous journey connects different media. Identity and behaviour from one stage feed into the next, so the effects of a label accumulate.

text.zh: 以问卷与面部输入作为身份生成的设计入口，形成虚构角色档案。
text.en: Questionnaire and facial inputs form the proposed entry point for generating a fictional profile.

text.zh: 通过词语选择、时间压力与带偏见的评分规则，把抽象的招聘判断变成可感知的反馈。
text.en: Word selection, time pressure, and biased scoring make abstract recruitment judgements tangible.

text.zh: 设计观众指令、评价与身体反馈之间的关系，探索 Kinect 与压力输入的可能性。
text.en: Design relationships between audience instructions, ratings, and bodily feedback, exploring Kinect and pressure inputs.

text.zh: 让积累的信息进入最终视觉结果，呈现一个人被观看和重构的过程。
text.en: Carry accumulated information into the final visual result, revealing how a person is viewed and reconstructed.

alt.zh: 虚拟直播表演舞台的全景。
alt.en: An overview of the virtual livestream performance stage.

caption.zh: 表演空间：用舞台、尺度与色彩强调身体被观看的处境。
caption.en: Performance space: stage, scale, and colour emphasise the body as an object of observation.

alt.zh: 紫色虚拟环境中的人物与空间。
alt.en: A figure within a purple virtual environment.

caption.zh: 虚拟场景探索：让情境从屏幕界面延伸到空间体验。
caption.en: Virtual environment exploration extends the scenario beyond a screen.

alt.zh: 项目中的竖屏直播界面视觉。
alt.en: The vertical livestream interface visual developed for the project.

caption.zh: 直播视觉：将空间表演与界面中的观看关系连接。
caption.en: Livestream visual: connecting spatial performance with interface-mediated viewing.

paragraphs.zh: 当前材料展示了研究转译、交互方案与视觉原型。它们说明设计如何把社会议题变成可体验的机制，但尚不足以证明参与者态度发生了改变。
paragraphs.en: The available material documents research translation, interaction concepts, and visual prototypes. These show how a social question can become an experience, but do not establish a change in participants’ attitudes.

paragraphs.zh: 下一步需要验证：参与者能否理解环节之间的数据关系，评分是否被理解为对偏见的呈现，以及退出与说明是否足够清晰。对敏感议题的表达，也需要邀请不同背景的参与者反馈。
paragraphs.en: Future evaluation should examine whether participants understand connections between stages, recognise scoring as a portrayal of bias, and can clearly exit or find explanations. Feedback from people with different backgrounds is also essential.
